chunks: Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he said:

The wergild (blood money) of the greyhound dog is forty dirhams, which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) established; and the wergild of the sheepdog is a ram; and the wergild of the field-guarding dog is a jarib of wheat; and the wergild of the domestic dog is a qafeez of soil from its owners.
ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for killing a dog in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details the specific financial compensation (*diyah*) for killing various types of dogs, distinguishing between the greyhound, sheepdog, field dog, and domestic dog. It attributes these valuations directly to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition of precise legal categorization in *fiqh*. The varying values highlight the functional and contextual significance of each dog type within early Islamic society.
